title: I built a free insider cluster detector using SEC Form 4 data — here's what it flagged this quarter
author: Cold-Fix-884
selftext:
I spent a few weeks building

a Python system that pulls Form 4 filings directly from EDGAR and detects

"cluster buys" — when 2+ insiders at the same company buy within a rolling

window.



Some findings from this quarter across \~100 megacap tickers:



\*\*Only 1 active cluster right now (60-day window):\*\*

\- BSX (Boston Scientific): 3 directors bought a combined $554,000 in mid-May

  \- Cheryl Pegus: 1,770 shares

  \- Edward Ludwig: 3,580 shares

  \- David Habiger: 4,450 shares

\- All within 48 hours of each other



\*\*Zero CEO/CFO open-market buys in the past 30 days\*\* across the universe.



\*\*What I learned building this:\*\*



1. \*\*Role weighting matters more than count.\*\* A 3-director cluster (weight

   3.0 in my system) is NOT the same signal as 1 CEO buy (weight 2.5).

   Kestrel's flat "N insiders" count throws away information.



2. \*\*60-day window > 30-day.\*\* The classic 30-day cluster window is too

   tight — you miss real signals because insider filings dribble in over

   weeks. 60 days catches actual buying campaigns without letting stale

   signals contaminate.



3. \*\*Transaction code P (open-market purchase) is the ONLY code worth

   scoring as a bullish signal.\*\* Codes A (grant), M (option exercise),

   F (tax withhold), G (gift) are noise. Codes S and D are sells.



4. \*\*Combining insider clusters with high short volume ("squeeze combos")

   is the highest-signal setup I found.\*\* BSX has an active cluster but

   only \~48% short volume — barely below the 50% threshold I use to flag.



\*\*Free data sources:\*\*

\- SEC EDGAR: submissions JSON at [data.sec.gov](http://data.sec.gov) (way better than the old

  atom feed, which returns 0 entries for Form 4 as of 2024)

\- FINRA: daily short-volume files at [cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/](http://cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/)

\- Google News RSS: chatter/velocity baseline



Whole pipeline runs on my local box, zero data cost.



Happy to answer questions about the Form 4 XML parsing gotchas (the

xslF345X06/ prefix thing burned me for a day) or the classification logic.
